page.title: Button
page.description: Triggers an action. Four variants, three sizes, every state built from semantic tokens.

overview.variantsBody: Four variants express how important an action is. Exactly one primary action per view.
overview.vPrimary: primary — the single most important action in a view. Never two at once.
overview.vSecondary: secondary — equally ranked side actions, such as Cancel next to a primary submit.
overview.vGhost: ghost — actions in dense areas: toolbars, table rows, card headers.
overview.vDanger: danger — destructive, irreversible actions only, always with a confirmation dialog.
overview.sizesBody: Type sizes stay on the scale: sm is text-xs (12px), md is text-sm (14px), lg is text-base (16px). The system has no in-between values.
overview.iconsBody: Icons come exclusively through the icon prop as Material Symbols Rounded. A leading icon describes the action, a trailing icon the direction.
overview.statesBody: The loading state keeps the variant colour and adds the spinner. Disabled buttons have their own resting surface per variant.
overview.fullWidthBody: fullWidth stretches the button across the container — the normal case for completing forms on mobile.
overview.hrefBody: With href an a element with role="button" is rendered. Use it for targets that should look like an action; for navigation within text, Link is the right choice.

usage.whenBody: For every action that changes, submits, opens or cancels something. For plain navigation within a text flow use Link, not Button.
usage.gPrimary: primary for the most common or most important next step — exactly once per view.
usage.gSecondary: secondary for the equally ranked alternative, such as Cancel next to Save.
usage.gGhost: ghost for actions that need no visual weight: toolbars and table rows.
usage.gDanger: danger only for deleting, removing and other irreversible steps.
usage.labelBody: Infinitive verb plus object: Termin anlegen, Profil speichern, Konto löschen. Not OK, not Weiter without context, not Absenden. German, formal address, no title case, no emoji.
usage.sizeChoiceBody: md at 40px is the normal case. lg at 48px completes forms and is the right choice on mobile. sm at 32px belongs in tables and toolbars — but never as the only hit target on touch devices, because 32px is below the 44px threshold.
usage.do1: Exactly one primary action per view.
usage.do2: Verb and object as the label, such as Konto anlegen.
usage.do3: danger only for destructive, irreversible actions.
usage.dont1: Several primary buttons side by side.
usage.dont2: Vague labels such as OK or Click here.
usage.dont3: ghost for the main action of a page.

a11y.focusBody: The focus ring is 3px and is never removed. The danger variant uses the red focus ring instead, so the ring does not fight the red surface — an approved exception.
a11y.k1: Tab and Shift+Tab move focus to the next or previous button.
a11y.k2: Enter and Space trigger the button.

a11y.aria1: With iconOnly an aria-label is mandatory — without a label the button is unnamed.
a11y.aria2: The loading state sets aria-busy="true" and keeps the variant colour.
a11y.aria3: Disabled buttons carry aria-disabled="true" so screen readers announce the state.
a11y.targetBody: On touch devices every button needs a surrounding area of at least 44 by 44 pixels. The sm size is below that and therefore belongs only in pointer contexts.

page.title: Link
page.description: Leads somewhere else. Two patterns: standalone without an underline, inline within body text.

overview.variantsBody: standalone stands on its own — at the end of a paragraph, in a card footer, next to a heading. Without an underline at rest, because its position makes it recognisable. inline sits within body text and is always underlined.
overview.sizesBody: Three sizes on the type scale: sm at 14px, md at 16px, lg at 20px. The size follows the text the link sits in.
overview.iconsBody: An icon after the text shows direction, an icon before it shows the kind of target. Trailing is the default position.
overview.externalBody: external sets the open_in_new glyph, target="_blank" and rel="noopener noreferrer". Always mark external targets — leaving the application should not come as a surprise.
overview.statesBody: Hover and active change the colour only. The underline stays as it is, and its thickness never changes in any state.

usage.vsButtonBody: A link navigates, a button acts. If the element leads to another page or view, it is a link. If it changes something, submits or opens a dialog, it is a button — even when it looks like a link. This distinction is not a matter of style: screen readers announce them differently, and a link can be opened in a new tab.
usage.pStandalone: standalone at the end of a paragraph, in card footers and next to headings.
usage.pInline: inline within body text — a link in text explained by colour alone is invisible to colour-blind readers.
usage.textBody: The text names the target: Barrierefreiheits-Richtlinien, not click here, not more. Link specific terms, not whole sentences — the underlined area is the hit target and should be as large as necessary, not as large as possible.
usage.disabledBody: A disabled link is a contradiction in itself. If a target is unreachable, show text without a link instead. disabled exists only for transitional states.
usage.dont1: Make links recognisable by colour alone.
usage.dont2: Use click here or more as link text.
usage.dont3: Link whole sentences.
usage.dont4: Use a link where an action is triggered.

code.iconDesc: Icons as a ligature name through icon, position through iconPosition:
code.externalDesc: External targets through the external prop:

a11y.colorBody: Within body text the underline carries recognisability, not the colour. That is why it stays in every state and never changes thickness.
a11y.focusBody: The focus ring is the usual 3px ring in the primary colour. It is never removed, not even for links in dense lists.
a11y.s1: A link without href is not a link to screen readers — actions belong in a button.
a11y.s2: External targets carry rel="noopener noreferrer" and a visible glyph as a warning.
a11y.s3: The link text works outside the sentence too, because screen readers read link lists without context.

page.title: Text input
page.description: Captures single-line free text. The basis for Number, Search, Select and Date picker — with a label on top or as a floating label, all states and optional features.

demo.label: Email address
demo.hint: We only use the address for appointment confirmations.
demo.error: The address is incomplete. Add the part after the @.

overview.anatomyBody: A text field is built from five parts. Label and input are always visible:
overview.an1: Label with required marker — always visible, tied to the input via htmlFor
overview.an2: Leading icon — decorative, flat in the field, without its own surface
overview.an4: Trailing icon — state indicator or an operable button
overview.an5: Message line — helper text, error or confirmation below the field
overview.statesBody: Eight states: resting, hover, focus, filled, disabled, read-only, error and success. The border stays 1px in every state — focus is carried by a 3px ring, so nothing shifts when the field is focused.
overview.statesNote: Hover and focus only show on interaction: move over a field or place the cursor inside it.
overview.sizesBody: sm 36px for dense tables and filter bars, md 40px as the normal case, lg 48px on mobile. Font sizes stay on the scale: 14 / 16 / 16.
overview.floatBody: The label sits inside the field and floats up into the border on focus or content. The field is 52px tall then. It is the exception for dense forms, not the rule — never mix it with fixed labels.
overview.featuresBody: Clear button, password toggle, character counter and fixed prefixes and suffixes. Operable icons carry button styling and an aria-label; decorative ones sit flat in the field.

usage.labelBody: The label is always visible. A placeholder is not a label — it disappears while typing and is then missing for exactly the person who needed it. The placeholder shows an example, not an instruction. Within one form use either required throughout or optional throughout, never both mixed.
usage.messageBody: At most one line sits below the field: error displaces success, success displaces hint. Error messages name the cause and the next step — “Please enter a valid email address.” instead of “Invalid input.” An error is never signalled by colour alone; there is always an icon and text.
usage.sizeBody: md is the normal case. lg belongs on mobile, because the hit target gets too small below it. sm only in dense tables and filter bars.
usage.widthBody: Field width follows the expected input — a postcode does not get a field spanning the whole column. prefix and suffix take fixed text parts out of the input (“https://”, “.de”, “€”) so nobody has to type them.
usage.iconBody: icon places a decorative glyph at the front — flat, without a surface. Operable icons look like small buttons instead (resting surface stone-100, hover stone-200) and always carry an aria-label: the clear button via clearable and the password toggle that type="password" brings along automatically. This is a fixed system rule, not a matter of style.
usage.readonlyBody: readOnly for values that are shown but not changed — customer number, generated ID. The field stays focusable and copyable and shows a lock. disabled only when the field does not apply under the current conditions. Confusing the two is the most common mistake.
usage.do1: Keep the label visible; never use the placeholder as a label.
usage.do2: Word the error concretely: what happened and what to do.
usage.do3: Match field width to the expected input.
usage.dont1: Don't put important information in the placeholder.
usage.dont2: No red alone — errors always with icon and text.
usage.dont3: Don't use disabled fields for read-only values.

a11y.labelBody: Every field gets an ID and a label with a matching htmlFor, so the screen reader announces the field name. With a floating label the association is kept — only the visual position changes.
a11y.errorBody: A set error puts aria-invalid="true" on the input, the message line carries role="alert" and is tied to the field via aria-describedby. Helper text and confirmation are associated the same way.
a11y.iconBody: Clear button and password toggle are real buttons with type="button" and an aria-label. They are reachable with the Tab key and show the same 3px ring on focus as the field.
a11y.focusBody: The focus ring is 3px in primary-600; in the error state it switches to error-600. The border stays 1px throughout, so nothing shifts on focus. All combinations are checked against WCAG 2.2 AA.

page.title: Number input
page.description: Captures numbers with stepper controls. Built on the text field: same anatomy, same states — plus up/down buttons, limits and step size.

demo.label: Number of packs
demo.hint: Arrow keys and the mouse wheel change the value by one step.
demo.error: The value exceeds the stock. Order at most 10 packs.

overview.variantsBody: chevrons puts both buttons on the right — the normal case at a desk. plusminus places minus on the left and plus on the right with a centred value; that is the touch variant with a larger hit target.
overview.sizesBody: sm 36px, md 40px, lg 48px — the same heights as the text field. Stepper width follows the size and stays the same in both variants.
overview.unitsBody: prefix and suffix show the unit fixed at the field so nobody types it along. align overrides the alignment — right-aligned is right when several numbers are compared below one another.
overview.statesBody: The same eight states as the text field. At a limit the matching button goes inactive instead of skipping past the value silently.

behavior.limits: min, max and step define limits and step size.
behavior.arrows: Arrow up and down change the value by one step.
behavior.wheel: The mouse wheel changes the value while the field has focus.

usage.whenBody: The number field belongs where values are adjusted in small steps — quantities, dosages, percentages. For very large ranges a free-text field is the better choice, because nobody clicks through a thousand steps with a stepper.
usage.variantBody: chevrons at the desk, plusminus on touch devices. Within one interface, stay with one variant.
usage.widthBody: Number fields do not span the whole column. width sets a fixed width matching the expected number of digits; fullWidth is the exception for narrow forms on mobile.
usage.do1: Use the stepper for small, frequent adjustments.
usage.do2: Set sensible limits via min and max.
usage.do3: Show the unit visibly at the field (kg, %, €).
usage.dont1: Not for very large ranges — use free text then.
usage.dont2: No buttons without a keyboard alternative.
usage.dont3: Don't skip past a limit silently.

a11y.roleBody: The input carries role="spinbutton" and reports the current value and its limits via aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax. A set error additionally puts aria-invalid="true" on it.
a11y.keyboardBody: Arrow up and arrow down change the value by one step — the steppers are therefore never the only way to operate the field. The value can also be typed directly; the field accepts both comma and full stop as a decimal separator.
a11y.stepperBody: Both buttons carry an aria-label (“Increase”, “Decrease”) and deliberately sit outside the tab order to keep the path through the form short. At a limit they go inactive.

page.title: Select
page.description: Selection from a known, closed list. Built on the text field — with groups, single and multiple selection.

demo.label: Specialty
demo.hint: Determines which forms are offered in the next step.
demo.error: Without a specialty the appointment cannot be assigned. Choose an entry.

overview.singleBody: The normal case: one value from a list. The dropdown appears in medo styling, is fully keyboard operable and opens upwards when there is no room below.
overview.multiBody: multiple turns the value into an array. The selection always stays on one line: as many chips are shown as fit into a line, the rest appears as a counter. multipleDisplay="count" replaces the chips entirely with “N selected”, maxChips sets a hard upper bound.
overview.searchBody: `searchable` shows a search field at the top of the panel and filters the list while typing, matching label and description. Group headings only remain while an entry below them survives; when nothing matches, the panel reports “No matches”. From about ten entries the search belongs there.
overview.flagNote: `flag` takes any CSS background value — a colour, a gradient, or `url(…)` for a real flag graphic. The swatch is 20 × 14 px. `description` sits as a second line below the label, for a country code, dialling code or postcode.
overview.headBody: With multiple selection the opened panel carries a header: the selection counter on the left, “Reset” on the right, which clears the whole selection in one step. Entries then show their state as a checkbox on the left instead of a check mark on the right — single selection keeps the check mark.
overview.groupBody: Entries can be bundled under headings. Group titles are not selectable and are skipped by keyboard navigation; individual entries can be inactive.
overview.sizesBody: sm 36px, md 40px, lg 48px — the same heights as the text field.
overview.statesBody: Error, success and disabled behave as on the text field. An empty option list shows a note instead of an empty menu.
overview.nativeBody: native switches to the operating system's picker. Right for very long lists and for forms that must work without JavaScript — the dropdown cannot be styled then.

native.label: Country
native.hint: The operating system provides the dropdown.

usage.whenBody: The select belongs to known, closed lists. Up to about five entries radio buttons are better — they show every option without a click. From about ten entries `searchable` shows a search inside the panel. When it is an open body of data rather than a closed list, the search field is right. For actions instead of values: the menu.
usage.orderBody: Sort by frequency or alphabetically, not randomly. Groups pay off from about ten entries; group titles name what was bundled.
usage.multiBody: Chips show the selection directly and can be removed one by one — right as long as the labels are short. With long labels or narrow fields the counter is calmer.
usage.searchBody: From about ten entries the search belongs there — below that it only costs an extra step. The search filters a known, closed list; it does not replace the search field, which searches an open body of data. With the search active the focus sits in the input, so the jump by first letter falls away.
usage.nativeBody: native is the right choice for very long lists and in forms that must work without JavaScript. The price is the unstylable dropdown — do not mix both modes within one form.
usage.do1: Sort entries by frequency or alphabetically.
usage.do2: Bundle into groups from about ten entries.
usage.do3: Prefer radio buttons for up to five entries.
usage.dont1: Don't use the list for an open body of data.
usage.dont2: No actions in the list — use the menu for those.
usage.dont3: Don't mix both modes within the same form.

a11y.roleBody: The field carries role="combobox" with aria-expanded, aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-controls. The menu is a role="listbox", each entry a role="option" with aria-selected; the active entry is reported via aria-activedescendant without the focus leaving the field. Multiple selection adds aria-multiselectable.
a11y.key1: Arrow up and down open the menu and move the active entry.
a11y.key2: Enter and Space select the active entry; with multiple selection they toggle it.
a11y.key3: Home and End jump to the first and last selectable entry.
a11y.key4: A single letter jumps to the first entry starting with it.
a11y.key5: Escape and Tab close the menu.
a11y.key6: With `searchable` the focus sits in the search field; the arrow keys drive the list from there.
a11y.key7: “Reset” in the header is a button of its own and reachable with the Tab key.
a11y.chipBody: Every remove cross on a chip carries an aria-label naming the entry (“Remove selection: Internal medicine”). The “+N” counter lists the hidden entries in its title attribute.

page.title: Search
page.description: Searches live while typing. Built on the field scaffold: leading magnifier, clear button and an optional suggestion panel with recent searches.

demo.label: Patient search
demo.hint: The search starts automatically as soon as you pause briefly.
demo.error: The search is currently unreachable. Try again in a few minutes.

overview.anatomyBody: The search field is a text field with a fixed division of roles:
overview.an1: Leading magnifier — decorative, replaced by a spinner while searching
overview.an2: Input — announces itself as a combobox for the suggestion panel
overview.an3: Clear button — appears as soon as something has been entered
overview.an4: Suggestion panel — recent searches and suggestions, keyboard operable
overview.panelBody: While the field is empty the panel shows recent searches. As soon as typing starts, suggestions take their place and the typed part is highlighted in the match. With onRemoveRecent, history entries get a remove button.
overview.emptyBody: When the search finds nothing, the panel names the query and says what helps next. emptyText replaces the default text with a more concrete hint.
overview.sizesBody: sm 36px, md 40px, lg 48px — the same heights as the text field.
overview.compactBody: compact is the flat variant for toolbars: 34px tall, without a border, on a filled surface. Without a label it stands on its own, with no field scaffold around it.
overview.statesBody: Resting, filled, searching, disabled, error and helper text. Focus carries the same 3px ring as every other field.

anatomy.label: Patient search
anatomy.hint: Search by name, date of birth or insurance number.

empty.text: Check the spelling or search by insurance number.

usage.whenBody: The search field belongs where one entry has to be found among many. For a known, closed list the select is right. As a pure filter field without suggestions, switch the panel off via showPanel.
usage.debounceBody: onSearch only fires after a short pause, 250 ms by default — not on every keystroke. It additionally fires immediately on Enter and when a suggestion is chosen. Adjust debounce when the search is expensive.
usage.panelBody: Recent searches only appear in the empty field — they are a starting point, not a result list. Keep the suggestion list short; more than about ten entries force scrolling instead of deciding.
usage.emptyBody: The empty state names the cause and the next step, not just the state. “Check the spelling or search by insurance number.” helps; “No results” does not.
usage.do1: Debounce the input instead of searching on every keystroke.
usage.do2: In the empty state, say what helps next.
usage.do3: Keep the suggestion list short and highlight the match.
usage.dont1: Don't style the magnifier as a button — it is decorative.
usage.dont2: Don't show recent searches while typing.
usage.dont3: Don't use the search field for closed lists.

a11y.roleBody: The input carries role="combobox" with aria-expanded, aria-autocomplete="list" and aria-controls pointing at the panel. The panel is a role="listbox", each entry a role="option" with aria-selected. Focus stays in the field while the arrow keys move through the entries.
a11y.key1: Arrow up and down open the panel and move the active entry.
a11y.key2: Enter accepts the active entry or starts the search immediately.
a11y.key3: Escape first clears the field and then closes the panel.
a11y.iconBody: The clear button and the remove cross in the history are real buttons with an aria-label (“Clear search”, “Remove from history”). The leading magnifier is decorative and hidden from screen readers; while searching, the spinner is hidden too.

page.title: Toggle
page.description: Switches a setting immediately. No save step, no confirmation.

demo.reminderDesc: Geht 24 Stunden vor dem Termin raus.
demo.videoDesc: Patientinnen und Patienten können online buchen.
demo.billingDesc: Rechnungen gehen am Monatsende automatisch raus.

overview.statesBody: Off is stone-300, on is the action colour. The thumb is always white and carries a check or a cross so the state does not hang on colour alone.
overview.sizesBody: Three sizes for different densities. The label only grows from 14px to 16px at lg.
overview.descriptionBody: The description explains the consequence of the on state, not how to operate it.
overview.labelLeftBody: In settings lists the label sits on the left and the switch at the end of the row. The control then fills the full width of the row.
overview.iconsBody: Check and cross in the thumb are the default and can be switched off where the control is very small or appears in large numbers.
overview.loadingBody: When saving takes noticeable time the thumb shows a spinner and operation is locked — without looking disabled. Try it: the example simulates saving.

usage.whenBody: For two states of a running setting that take effect immediately: notifications on, profile visible, reminder active. If the change needs a submit step or belongs to a form that gets saved, it is a checkbox — not a toggle.
usage.labelBody: The label names the on state (“Benachrichtigungen”), not the action (“Benachrichtigungen einschalten”). No “on/off” text next to it — the switch shows that itself.
usage.loadingBody: The switch moves to the new position immediately and is only reverted if the server rejects it — and then with a visible message. Switching without feedback when the operation can fail is the one thing that must not happen here.
usage.dont1: Use it as a form field that only takes effect on save.
usage.dont2: Use two toggles for an either-or choice — that is what Radio is for.
usage.dont3: Phrase the label as an action.
usage.dont4: Switch without feedback when the operation can fail.

code.basicDesc: Uncontrolled with a starting value through defaultChecked:
code.controlledDesc: Controlled through checked and onChange — onChange receives the new state as a boolean, not an event:
code.settingsDesc: In settings lists the label sits on the left:

a11y.roleBody: Rendered as a button with role="switch" and aria-checked. Without a label an aria-label is mandatory.
a11y.k1: Tab moves focus; the 3px ring sits around the track.
a11y.s1: The loading state sets aria-busy="true" and locks operation.
a11y.s2: The state does not hang on colour alone: check and cross in the thumb carry it too.
a11y.s3: Sizes sm and md are below 44px — in touch lists the row provides the hit target, standalone use lg.

page.title: Checkbox
page.description: Multiple selection: none to many options. Custom graphics so colour, radius and focus ring come from the tokens.

demo.reminderHint: Die Erinnerung geht 24 Stunden vorher raus.
demo.releaseHint: Die Praxis sieht den Befund sofort.

overview.statesBody: Checked and indeterminate share the same surface in the action colour and differ by their mark: check versus dash. The error state colours the border only.
overview.sizesBody: Box 18px (sm) or 20px (md), radius 4px, border 1px. The label stays at 14px in both sizes.
overview.hintBody: The hint sits below the label and explains the consequence of the choice — not how to operate it.
overview.groupBody: Checkboxes belong in a group with a legend, otherwise a screen reader cannot tell what the options belong to. The header sits in the indeterminate state while only some of the options below are selected.
overview.horizontalBody: Vertical is the normal case. Horizontal only for two or three very short labels.

usage.w1: For none-to-many options from a list.
usage.w2: A single checkbox is right for consent — acknowledging a declaration, for example.
usage.w3: For two states that take effect immediately use a Toggle; for exactly one option out of several use a Radio.
usage.labelBody: The label belongs inside the label element so the whole row is a hit target. On touch devices the row must be at least 44px high.
usage.indeterminateBody: Indeterminate means “some below are selected” — typical for the header of a tree selection or a table column. It is not a third value for “unknown” and is never set without a selection underneath.
usage.errorBody: Leaving a required consent without an error message helps nobody: the error state colours the border and sets aria-invalid, and the reason belongs next to it.
usage.dont1: Group without a legend.
usage.dont2: Use the indeterminate state as a value of its own.
usage.dont3: Use it for on/off switches that take effect immediately.

code.title: Checkbox in code
code.basicDesc: Label through label, second line through hint:
code.groupDesc: Groups take a legend and a direction:
code.indeterminateDesc: The indeterminate state derives from the state of the children:

a11y.labelBody: The component renders a label element around the native input — the label is part of the hit target without an id link and is read out by screen readers.
a11y.k1: Tab moves focus to the box; the ring sits 3px around it.
a11y.s1: The indeterminate state is set as a DOM property on the native input, not just visually — screen readers announce it as “partially checked”.
a11y.s3: Disabled boxes are not focusable; the reason belongs visibly on the page.

page.title: Radio
page.description: Single selection: exactly one option out of a manageable set.

billing.privateHint: Rechnung direkt an die Patientin oder den Patienten.

overview.statesBody: At rest the circle carries the input border colour, selected the action colour, on hover one step darker. Disabled and selected shows a stone-400 dot in a muted circle — not the action colour.
overview.sizesBody: Circle 18px (sm) or 20px (md), dot 9px and 10px respectively, border 1px.
overview.groupBody: The group is the normal case: it generates the shared name itself when none is set and takes the options as an array. A legend is mandatory, otherwise screen readers lack the context.
overview.hintBody: A hint below the option explains what the choice means. It does not replace a clear label.
overview.horizontalBody: Vertical is the normal case; horizontal only for two or three short labels.
overview.cardBody: The card variant renders the options as selection cards: title on the left, dot on the right, explanation below. The selected card gets border and surface in the primary colour, and the whole card is clickable.

usage.whenBody: For two to about five equally ranked options that should all be visible. Beyond that use Select. For none-to-many use Checkbox. For a switch that takes effect immediately use Toggle.
usage.g1: A group legend is mandatory — without it screen readers lack the context.
usage.g2: Individual radios outside a group need a manually set, shared name, otherwise they do not exclude each other.
usage.g3: Preselect when one option is the safe default. If there is none, leave everything empty — a wrong preselection is worse than none, because it is adopted unnoticed.
usage.cardBody: Cards are meant for few, weighty alternatives that need a description — tariffs, shipping methods, visibility levels. Three to four cards is the maximum; beyond that the row gets crowded and the list form is better.
usage.dont1: Group without a legend.
usage.dont2: Scatter radios without a shared name.
usage.dont3: Use a single radio that cannot be deselected — that is what the checkbox is for.
usage.dont4: List more than about five options.

code.groupDesc: The group takes the options as an array:
code.cardDesc: The card variant needs options; hint becomes the explanation below the title:
code.childrenDesc: Instead of the shorthand, individual radios can be passed as children:

a11y.groupBody: The group renders a fieldset with role="radiogroup" and the legend as its label. Screen readers announce on entry what the options belong to.
a11y.k1: Tab enters the group — on the selected option, otherwise on the first.
a11y.k2: Arrow keys move within the group and select as they go.
a11y.k3: Tab leaves the group as a whole instead of stepping through every option.
a11y.s1: The error state sets aria-invalid="true" on the affected input.
a11y.s2: Disabled options stay visible but take no focus — the reason belongs visibly next to them.

page.title: Tag
page.description: Marks, categorises or filters. Six colour roles, two styles, always fully rounded.

overview.colorsBody: Six roles: neutral, primary, success, warning, error and info. A colour means the same thing across the whole product — green not once for active and once for paid.
overview.sizesBody: 22px (sm) belongs in table rows and dense lists, 28px (md) everywhere else. The radius is always full — that tells tags apart from buttons at a glance.
overview.dotIconBody: Dot and icon help with scanning but never replace a label. The text always carries the meaning.
overview.removableBody: onRemove adds a remove button — meant for selected filters that can be taken off one by one. removeLabel names what is being removed.
overview.selectableBody: selectable renders a button with aria-pressed — for filter bars where tags are switched on and off. The selected state additionally shows a check mark.

usage.tDisplay: Display is the normal case: not operable, carries status or category.
usage.tRemovable: Removable comes from onRemove — for selected filters.
usage.tSelectable: Selectable comes from selectable — for filter bars with on and off.
usage.typesNote: A tag is not a button. If the element triggers an action beyond selected and not selected, a button belongs there.
usage.colorBody: soft (surface 50) is the default and works in quantity. solid (solid colour 600) is loud and belongs used sparingly — at most one or two per view. Neutral is the right choice when a tag only names and does not judge.
usage.textBody: One or two words. Longer text is truncated because a tag does not wrap — if the text cannot be kept short, it is not a tag.
usage.sizeBody: On touch devices removable and selectable tags need a surrounding area at least 44px high.
usage.dont1: Misuse tags as buttons for actions.
usage.dont2: Show more than two or three colour roles at once on one surface.
usage.dont3: Carry meaning through colour alone.
usage.dont4: Put whole sentences into a tag.

code.title: Tag in code
code.basicDesc: Colour role through color, style through emphasis, status dot through dot:
code.removeDesc: Removable through onRemove; removeLabel names the button:

a11y.meaningBody: Meaning must never hang on colour alone. The text carries it; dot and icon are an addition, not a replacement.
a11y.c1: The remove button always carries an aria-label naming what is removed.
a11y.c2: Selectable tags are buttons with aria-pressed, operable via Tab, Enter and Space.
a11y.c3: Disabled selectable tags stay visible but accept no input.
a11y.targetBody: The remove button is 18px (sm) or 20px. On touch devices its surrounding area needs at least 44px of height, otherwise it cannot be hit reliably.

page.description: Alert — an inline status message in four semantic variants for information, success, warning, and error.

overview.anatomyBody: An alert consists of an icon, optional title, and message text — embedded in a colored, semantically styled container.
overview.an2: Title — optional, bold; summarizes the message
overview.an3: Message — the actual notification text (children prop)
overview.an4: Container — colored background with matching border color
overview.variantsBody: Four semantic variants: info (blue), success (green), warning (yellow), error (red). Each has its own icon, background, and border color.

usage.title: Usage
usage.intro: Alerts provide directly visible feedback on user actions or system events — inline on the page, not as transient toast messages.
usage.infoWhen: info — general hints, neutral system messages, explanations
usage.warningWhen: warning — reversible risks, stale data, soon-expiring sessions
usage.errorWhen: error — failures, failed actions, validation errors
usage.placementBody: Alerts appear inline in the content area — directly above the affected form section or at the top of a page. For transient notifications, Toast is more appropriate.
usage.do1: Choose variant semantically — error only for real errors, not for hints
usage.do2: Write short, action-oriented text — what happened, what to do?
usage.do3: Use a title when the message spans more than one sentence
usage.dont1: Don't use Alert as a decorative element
usage.dont2: No long body text in alerts — maximum 2–3 sentences
usage.dont3: Don't use Alert for success feedback after form submit — Toast is more visible
usage.doNote: Clear, action-oriented messages help users respond quickly.
usage.dontNote: Too many alerts on one page lead to alert fatigue.

code.title: Code
code.variantsDesc: The variant prop automatically determines icon, background color, and border color.
code.noTitleDesc: The title prop is optional. Without a title, only the children text is shown.
code.inlineDesc: Place the Alert above the form or after the submit button for error and success feedback.
code.toastDesc: Toast is a separate component for transient messages. It typically appears at the screen edge and disappears after a short time.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: Alerts are inline and immediately visible. For dynamically inserted alerts, live region support is critical.
a11y.roleBody: The Alert component automatically sets role="alert". Screen readers announce the content immediately when it is inserted into the DOM.
a11y.colorTitle: Color is not the only indicator
a11y.colorBody: Each variant combines icon, color, and text — colorblind users recognize the variant by icon and content, not color alone.
a11y.focusBody: Alerts do not receive focus automatically. For critical error messages, programmatically call focus() on the alert container.
a11y.k1: Tab — make the alert container focusable via tabIndex={0}
a11y.k2: Screen reader — reads role="alert" content immediately upon DOM insertion

page.description: Flexible container component with a compound API of Card.Header, Card.Body, and Card.Footer.

overview.anatomyBody: A card consists of up to three optional sections that together form a structured content unit.
overview.an1: Card.Header — title, optional subtitle, and optional actions on the right
overview.an2: Card.Body — main content: text, forms, lists, or other components
overview.an4: variant prop — flat (default, with border) or raised (shadow, no border)
overview.variantsBody: The four most common configurations: flat with footer, raised with footer, no footer, and header with action button.
overview.flatBody: Card content — text, data, forms, or other components.
overview.raisedBody: Raised cards stand out through a shadow effect. Suitable for panels that should appear visually in the foreground.
overview.noFooterBody: When no actions are required, Card.Footer can be omitted.
overview.actionBody: Card.Header optionally accepts children for actions — right-aligned next to title and subtitle.

usage.title: When to use cards?
usage.intro: Cards suit discrete content units that should be visually separated from the rest of the page — e.g. products, user profiles, dashboard panels, or form containers.
usage.compoundBody: All three sections are optional. Combine them as needed:
usage.partHeader: Title and optional subtitle, optional actions on the right (e.g. button, icon)
usage.partBody: Main content — no restrictions on what can be placed here
usage.do1: Use Card as a container for related content
usage.do2: Use flat for standard layouts, raised for highlighted panels
usage.do3: Only use Card.Footer when actions are present
usage.dont1: No onClick directly on Card — place interactive elements in Card.Body or Footer
usage.dont2: No deeply nested cards (Card in Card) — avoid layout complexity
usage.dont3: Don't use Card as a purely decorative frame without content
usage.doNote: Cards structure content — they don't replace it.
usage.dontNote: Cards are containers, not interactive elements.

code.title: Code Examples
code.flatDesc: Standard card with header, body, and footer buttons.
code.raisedDesc: Elevated variant with shadow — no border.
code.actionDesc: Card.Header optionally accepts children for actions right of the title.
code.formDesc: Cards work well as structured form containers with submit actions in the footer.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: Cards are semantically neutral div containers. Accessibility depends on the content — particularly the heading hierarchy and focusable elements.
a11y.headingBody: Card.Header renders the title as a div, not a heading element. Use an appropriate heading level (h2–h4) inside Card.Body if the card is part of a documented hierarchy.
a11y.focusBody: All interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs) inside the card are reachable via Tab. The card itself receives no focus.
a11y.clickBody: Card is not an interactive element. An onClick on the outer card would not be operable for keyboard and screen reader users. Actions belong in Card.Footer or Card.Body.

page.description: Structured data table with configurable columns and optional render functions for custom cell content.

overview.anatomyBody: The Table component consists of a header row and any number of data rows. Each column is defined via a columns array.
overview.an1: Header row — generated from columns[].label, uppercase with letter-spacing
overview.an2: Data row — from rows[] objects; each cell reads row[col.key]
overview.an3: render function — optional col.render(row) for custom cell content (e.g. Badge, Button)
overview.an4: rowKey — prop for the React key, defaults to 'id'
overview.demoBody: 5 rows, 4 columns — the status column uses a render function with a Badge component.
overview.hoverBody: Each row has a group-hover effect: hovering sets the background to surface-alt. This improves readability in long tables.

usage.title: When to use tables?
usage.intro: Tables suit structured data lists where users want to compare or scan values column by column.
usage.when1: User lists, products, orders — each entity has identical attributes
usage.when2: Comparison data where users scan values in a column
usage.when3: Tables with per-row actions (Edit, Delete) via render function
usage.renderBody: When a column needs more than plain text — e.g. Badge for status, Button for actions, Link for navigation — pass a render function. render receives the entire row object.
usage.do1: Set rowKey to the unique primary key field of your data
usage.do2: Use render functions for status badges, action buttons, or links
usage.do3: Limit column count to essentials — max 6–7 columns
usage.dont1: No nested tables (Table inside Table)
usage.dont2: No image-only cells without a text alternative
usage.dont3: Don't set rowKey to a non-unique value (e.g. index)
usage.doNote: Tables for tabular data — not as a layout grid.
usage.dontNote: Images as the sole cell content are meaningless to screen readers.

code.title: Code Examples
code.baseDesc: Minimal configuration with columns and rows.
code.renderDesc: Badge in the status column and Button in the action column via col.render(row).
code.rowKeyDesc: When the primary key is not 'id', pass it explicitly via rowKey.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: The Table component renders semantic HTML: table, thead, tbody, th, td. Screen readers recognize the table structure automatically.
a11y.roleBody: table/thead/tbody/th/td elements are implicitly marked with role="table", role="rowgroup", role="columnheader", and role="cell" — no explicit ARIA needed.
a11y.scopeBody: All th elements have scope="col" — screen readers can correctly associate cells with column headers.
a11y.keyboardBody: Tab navigates through all focusable elements inside the table (buttons, links). Rows themselves are not focusable.
a11y.srBody: Images or icons as the sole cell content need an aria-label or alt attribute so screen readers understand the context.

page.title: Tabs
page.description: Switching between equal views of the same object — the same person, the same file, a different view of it.

demo.panel: The content of the active tab goes here. Spacing, surface, and radius are set by the page, not by the component.

overview.variantsBody: underline is the normal case for tabs that structure a page area; the indicator sits below the active tab and there is no continuous baseline. contained rests on a stone-100 bar and is meant for tabs inside a card or next to a toolbar, where an underline would clash with the card edge.
overview.panelBody: Children are rendered as the role="tabpanel" of the active tab and stay unstyled. The panel content is remounted on every switch — state that should survive the switch belongs outside.
overview.verticalBody: With many areas the vertical form is the calmer solution. It sits to the left of the panel and always follows the underline logic; the indicator moves to the left edge.
overview.scrollBody: From about seven tabs on, set scrollable: the bar scrolls horizontally instead of wrapping, without a visible scrollbar.
overview.fullWidthBody: fullWidth divides the width evenly between the tabs. Use it only when the tabs span a card or sheet completely — on wide pages the labels drift far apart otherwise.
overview.sizesBody: md is the default, sm condenses bar and labels for cards and toolbars.

usage.whenBody: For equal views of the same object. When it is about the presentation of the same list — list, grid, kanban — it is a ContentSwitcher. When it is about steps in a sequence, a ProgressIndicator.
usage.styleBody: underline structures a page area, contained sits in a card or next to a toolbar. Never mix the two on the same level.
usage.labelBody: One or two words per label, no sentences. A badge carries a count only — no status word and no “new”.
usage.stateBody: Without value the component manages the selection itself. With value and onChange it lives outside — necessary when the address or other parts of the interface should follow along.
usage.do1: Show equal views of the same subject
usage.do2: Set scrollable from about seven tabs on, vertical with many areas
usage.do3: Keep labels to one or two words
usage.dont1: Map steps or a sequence onto tabs
usage.dont2: Nest tabs — a second level is not shown as tabs
usage.dont3: Submit something on switching; tabs show, they do not save

a11y.rolesBody: The bar is role="tablist" with aria-orientation, each tab role="tab" with aria-selected. When children are present they are rendered as role="tabpanel" and connected to the active tab via aria-controls and aria-labelledby.
a11y.key1: Arrow keys — switch directly, the selection follows the focus
a11y.key2: Home and End — jump to the edges
a11y.key4: Only the active tab is in the tab order; from there Tab leads on into the panel
a11y.badgeBody: The counter sits inside the tab label and is read out with it. That is why it carries a count only — a status word could not be attributed at this position.

page.title: Content Switcher
page.description: Switches the presentation of the same content — list, grid, kanban; month, quarter, year. The subject stays the same, only the view changes.

icon.sharedState: Both bars share the same state — what you pick in one also shows in the other.

overview.variantsBody: neutral rests on a stone-100 bar, the active segment is white with shadow-sm — the default case, calm enough for toolbars. outline shares a border and fills the active segment with primary-600; useful when the bar sits on an already tinted surface where the neutral track disappears.
overview.iconBody: iconOnly is allowed only for generally known presentations. The label then becomes the aria-label and appears on hover or focus as a dark hint above the segment — an additional tooltip is unnecessary and would appear twice.
overview.widthBody: All segments are equally wide so that nothing jumps on switching. equalWidth={false} ties the width to the text — then the bar changes shape on every switch. fullWidth stretches it across the available width.
overview.sizesBody: md measures 40 px in height, sm 32 px. sm belongs in toolbars, md stands on its own above content.
overview.statesBody: Disabled segments stay visible and are skipped by the arrow keys. In the outline form they also carry a tinted surface.

usage.whenBody: When the view of the same content changes. When whole views of an object alternate, they are Tabs. When the click triggers an action, it is a Button. When it is a setting that gets saved, they are Radio options — the content switcher always switches immediately and saves nothing.
usage.countBody: Two to five segments. More becomes a Select — a bar that has to scroll is no longer a bar.
usage.labelBody: One word per segment. With iconOnly the icon must be understandable without explanation; icons you have to guess do not belong in a bar without text.
usage.widthBody: equalWidth is the default and should stay that way. Tie the width to the text and the bar jumps on every switch — exactly what it is meant to prevent.
usage.do1: Use it to switch the presentation of the same content
usage.do2: Two to five segments, one word per segment
usage.do3: Keep the segments equally wide
usage.dont1: Use it as a filter with several simultaneous values — those are selectable tags
usage.dont2: Show more than five segments
usage.dont3: Use icon-only with icons you have to guess

a11y.rolesBody: The bar is role="tablist", each segment role="tab" with aria-selected. The matching content is rendered by the page and carries role="tabpanel". ariaLabel names what is being switched.
a11y.key1: Arrow keys — switch directly between segments
a11y.key2: Home and End — jump to the edges
a11y.key3: Only the active segment is in the tab order, disabled ones are skipped
a11y.iconOnlyBody: With iconOnly the label becomes the segment's aria-label and also appears visibly on hover and focus. The hint itself is aria-hidden so it is not read out twice.

page.title: Breadcrumb
page.description: Shows the path to the current page and leads back. It is orientation, not navigation for the next step.

overview.anatomyBody: The first level is the root, the last one the current page:
overview.an1: The current page is not a link, sits in text-muted, and carries aria-current="page"
overview.an2: The separator is a slash in stone-400 — no chevron, no arrows
overview.an3: The labels are the real page titles; a level truncates with an ellipsis at about 220 px
overview.collapseBody: From maxItems on, the middle collapses into a … menu: first level, “…”, the last two levels. The menu opens on click and closes on a click outside or with Esc. The first and the current level are never hidden — those two carry the orientation.
overview.iconBody: homeIcon replaces the label of the first level with the house icon. Individual levels can carry their own icon when it makes the level quicker to recognise.
overview.sizesBody: sm is the default above a page heading, md stands on its own in a header.

usage.whenBody: As soon as content sits at least three levels deep and can be entered directly from outside. On first-level pages it is superfluous — there only the title stands. It never replaces the browser's back button and never a visible main navigation.
usage.labelBody: The labels are the real page titles. No invented short forms — shortening a level makes the path unreadable.
usage.collapseBody: As soon as the path would run past one line. maxItems={0} turns collapsing off; that only makes sense for short, fixed paths.
usage.currentBody: The last level is deliberately not a link and not focusable. It says where you are, not where you can go.
usage.do1: Use it from three levels on, with the real page titles
usage.do2: Collapse the middle into the … menu on long paths
usage.do3: Keep the current page as the last level without a link
usage.dont1: Render the current page as a link
usage.dont2: Use the breadcrumb as a replacement for tabs or a menu
usage.dont3: Insert levels that do not exist as pages

a11y.structureBody: The bar is a nav with aria-label and contains an ol. The separators are aria-hidden so screen readers do not read out slashes. Every level is a link or a button with a focus ring.
a11y.currentBody: The last level carries aria-current="page" and is deliberately not focusable — it leads nowhere.
a11y.menuBody: The button carries its own label and aria-expanded. The opened menu is role="menu" with role="menuitem" per entry and closes on a click outside or with Esc.

page.title: Code Snippet
page.description: Present code readably and copyably — inline in text, as a single line, as a block with line numbers, or as terminal output.

overview.variantsBody: inline sits in running text on a light surface — for single commands and identifiers, without a copy button. single is one line with copying. block has a header bar with a language label and copying, line numbers in the gutter, and collapses from eight lines on. terminal shows three dots instead of the language label and sets $ prompts in green.
overview.highlightBody: Six colours, and no more: keywords, strings, numbers, comments in italics, calls, and the prompt. highlight={false} turns them off — useful for output that has no language.
overview.numbersBody: Line numbers sit in their own gutter and are hidden from screen readers. On short excerpts they cost more attention than they help — then use showLineNumbers={false}.
overview.collapseBody: From collapseAfter lines on, the block collapses and shows below how many lines there are in total. The default is eight lines; terminal output never collapses.
overview.copyBody: The button sits at the right of the header bar and confirms for about 1.5 seconds in green. An invisible aria-live region also reports the success — no notification is needed for that.

usage.whenBody: For code that is meant to be read or taken over. Running text and messages do not belong in a code block — there they lose their readability and suggest they have to be typed out.
usage.darkBody: Block and terminal sit on #211f1c — the only dark surface in the system. That is deliberate: code should stand out from the rest of the interface.
usage.colorBody: The six syntax colours are the whole set. Inventing further colours for keywords or types makes the code more colourful, but not more readable.
usage.copyBody: Every form except inline carries it. On inline it would be larger than the content and would stand in the middle of a sentence.
usage.do1: Show blocks with a language label
usage.do2: Let long blocks collapse
usage.do3: Use inline for single commands and identifiers in running text
usage.dont1: Put running text or messages into a code block
usage.dont2: Invent your own colours for keywords
usage.dont3: Attach a copy button to inline

a11y.liveBody: The success is announced through an invisible region with role="status" and aria-live="polite". Screen readers hear the confirmation without a notification interrupting the flow.
a11y.gutterBody: The gutter with the line numbers is aria-hidden and not selectable. Copying from the page therefore does not carry the numbers into the text.
a11y.contrastBody: The syntax colours are checked against the dark surface. They never carry a message on their own — the meaning is in the code itself, not in its colouring.

page.description: Modal dialog for confirmations, forms, and detail views — locks the background and manages focus automatically.

overview.anatomyBody: The Modal is based on Radix UI Dialog and consists of five sections:
overview.an1: Overlay — semi-transparent background; clicking it closes the modal
overview.an2: DialogContent — white panel, centered, with configurable width (size prop)
overview.an3: DialogHeader — title row at the top of the modal
overview.an4: children — main content: text, forms, or other components
overview.an5: DialogFooter — optional action row at the bottom (footer prop)
overview.demoBody: Open modals via button. Close via Escape, overlay click, or the close button.
overview.demoSmBody: This modal uses size="sm" — max width 384 px. Suitable for brief confirmations.
overview.demoMdBody: size="md" is the default — max width 512 px. For forms and medium-length content.
overview.demoLgBody: size="lg" — max width 672 px. For complex content, tables, or extensive forms.

usage.title: When to use Modal?
usage.intro: Modals interrupt the workflow — only use them when a direct user response is required.
usage.when1: Confirmation dialogs for irreversible actions (Delete, Publish)
usage.when2: Forms that require a standalone context (Invite, Create)
usage.when3: Detail views that should be accessible without a page change
usage.whenNotBody: Don't use Modal for simple status messages — use the Alert component. Don't use Modal for complex navigation or multi-step workflows — prefer a dedicated page or Stepper.
usage.do1: Use a clear title that names the action (e.g. 'Delete entry?')
usage.do2: Always offer a way to close: X button, Escape, overlay click
usage.do3: Match modal size to content (sm for confirmations, lg for forms)
usage.dont1: Don't open modals inside modals
usage.dont2: No auto-close without user action for critical dialogs
usage.dont3: Don't put long body text without a scroll container in the modal
usage.doNote: Modals for decisions — not for information.
usage.dontNote: No modal for messages the user doesn't need to confirm.

code.title: Code Examples
code.baseDesc: Minimal modal: open state, onClose handler, title, and children.
code.confirmDesc: footer prop for action buttons — Cancel on the left, destructive action on the right.
code.sizeDesc: size prop: sm (384px), md (512px, default), lg (672px).

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: Radix UI Dialog fully implements the WAI-ARIA Dialog Pattern: focus trapping, Escape, role="dialog", aria-modal.
a11y.k2: Tab / Shift+Tab — cycle focus within the modal (focus trap)
a11y.k3: Click on overlay — close the modal
a11y.focusBody: When opened, focus jumps automatically into the modal (first focusable element). When closed, focus returns to the triggering button.
a11y.roleBody: DialogContent has role="dialog" and aria-modal="true". Screen readers know the background is inactive and only read the modal content.
a11y.overlayBody: Clicking the overlay closes the modal via onOpenChange. This behavior can be disabled by removing the handler (e.g. for mandatory dialogs).
a11y.wcagBody: The modal dialog follows a logical Tab order: first focusable content → footer buttons → X button. No focus escapes outside the modal.

page.title: Accordion
page.description: Folds sections open and closed. It saves space for content that is not all needed at once — not a way to tidy up an overcrowded page.

demo.i1Content: The registration was verified on 12.03.2026. The agent number is D-4F2K-9TQ8L-24 and is valid until 31.12.2027.
demo.i2Content: Sum insured 1.500.000,00 € per claim. Proof is on file until 30.06.2027.
demo.i3Content: The next premium of 1.234,56 € will be collected on 04.08.2026. A change of payment method takes effect from the following due date.

faq.q1: How do I change my payment method?
faq.a1: Open the contract and choose “Change payment method”. The change takes effect from the next due date.
faq.q2: When do I receive my confirmation?
faq.a2: The confirmation is available in your inbox no later than two working days after conclusion.
faq.a3: Yes. Add further locations in the practice details; each location receives its own number.

overview.anatomyBody: Each section consists of a header acting as a button and a content area that grows via grid-template-rows from 0fr to 1fr — with no fixed height and no jump.
overview.an1: title — a statement, not a question, except in genuine FAQs
overview.an2: subtitle — second line in the header, short and explanatory
overview.an3: meta — brief note to the right of the marker, such as “3 entries”
overview.an4: icon — ligature name of a Material Symbols Rounded icon on the left of the header
overview.variantsBody: card places all sections in one card with dividers, separated sets each section as its own card, plain shows only lines without a frame.
overview.behaviourBody: multiple is the default: expanding closes nothing that is currently being read. Use multiple={false} only when the sections exclude one another. showToggleAll adds “Expand all / Collapse all” — useful for long lists, unnecessary with three sections.
overview.markerBody: Plus and minus are the default. The rotating chevron is the alternative when plus and minus already carry another meaning nearby. The two are never mixed on one page.
overview.sizesBody: md is the default, sm condenses header and content for data-heavy areas.
overview.faqBody: For questions and answers, separated cards with a chevron and only one open section work well.

usage.whenBody: For secondary content read one piece at a time: questions and answers, detail blocks of a form, optional entries. Whatever is needed to work stays open.
usage.whenNotBody: Not for content that has to be compared — show everything open instead. Not for navigation (use ContainedList or Tabs) and not for steps in a sequence (use ProgressIndicator). An accordion in which everything has to be expanded was the wrong choice.
usage.headerBody: The title is a statement, not an action: “Professional liability” instead of “Show details”. subtitle explains, meta counts.
usage.toggleAllBody: showToggleAll appears only with multiple. Use it for long lists; with three sections it costs more attention than it saves.
usage.do1: Use it for secondary, groupable content that should save space
usage.do2: Use multiple={false} for sections that exclude one another
usage.do3: Keep headers short and unambiguous
usage.dont1: Collapse required entries or error messages
usage.dont2: Nest an accordion inside an accordion
usage.dont3: Use an accordion for a single section — that is a paragraph with a heading

a11y.rolesBody: The header is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, the content a role="region" with aria-labelledby. Disabled sections are real disabled buttons.
a11y.key1: Enter or Space — expand or collapse the section
a11y.key2: Arrow up and down — move between headers, disabled ones are skipped
a11y.key3: Home and End — jump to the first or last header
a11y.domBody: Collapsed sections remain in the document. Browser search finds their content even when it is not visible.

page.title: Dropdown
page.description: A trigger with a menu. MenuList is the shared menu surface of the system — context menu and menu buttons use it too.

overview.triggerBody: The button carries a label and a chevron, the kebab only an icon without a border. The kebab belongs in table rows and card headers where there is no room for a label — it then needs an ariaLabel.
overview.sizesBody: Two sizes: sm at 32px for dense areas, md at 40px as the normal case. The menu surface itself stays the same in both.
overview.alignBody: The menu aligns to the left or right of the trigger. At the right edge of the screen use end, otherwise the surface runs out of view.
overview.entriesBody: An entry carries a label and optionally an icon, a shortcut and a state. Structure comes from two dedicated types.
overview.e1: icon places a Material symbol on the left, shortcut a key hint on the right in DM Mono.
overview.e2: danger colours text and icon red — that entry belongs at the end.
overview.e3: disabled locks the entry; it stays visible but takes no focus.
overview.e4: type: divider separates groups, type: heading labels them.
overview.e5: href renders the entry as a link instead of a button.
overview.subTitle: Submenu
overview.subBody: An entry with its own items opens a submenu — one level, no more. It opens on hover and with the right arrow key; the left arrow closes it again.
overview.selectionBody: With a selection mode every entry gets a check column and the matching ARIA role. For multiple selection keepOpen keeps the menu open so several entries can be toggled in a row.
overview.menuListBody: The menu surface can be used without a trigger — shown here without auto focus so the page does not jump on load. Context menu and menu buttons use it the same way.
overview.disabledBody: A disabled trigger stays visible and does not open. If the action does not belong in this view at all, remove it rather than showing it disabled.

usage.whenBody: For a handful of equally ranked actions that need not all be permanently visible. If it is about choosing a value for a form, use Select — the dropdown triggers actions, it does not fill a field.
usage.o1: The most common action goes on top.
usage.o2: Groups come from dividers, not from blank lines.
usage.o3: Destructive actions go at the bottom, separated and in danger.
usage.labelBody: Infinitive verb plus object, as with the button. The trigger names the group of actions, not the first of them.
usage.dont1: Put more than about eight entries on one surface.
usage.dont2: Nest submenus — one level is the maximum.
usage.dont3: Use a kebab without an ariaLabel.
usage.dont4: Use the dropdown as a replacement for a select field.

code.basicDesc: Trigger and entries; onSelect receives the value and the whole entry:
code.entriesDesc: The fields of an entry and the two structural types:
code.subDesc: A submenu comes from items on the entry itself:
code.selectionDesc: Selection mode with a check column:
