a11y.k1: Arrow down opens the menu from the trigger; on opening, focus sits on the first entry.
a11y.k2: Arrow up and down move between entries and wrap around at the ends.
a11y.k3: Home and End jump to the first and last entry.
a11y.k4: Typing jumps to the entry whose label matches — several characters within 800ms count as one search term.
a11y.k5: Enter or Space selects, Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger.
a11y.r1: The surface carries role=menu, every entry role=menuitem.
a11y.r2: In selection mode these become menuitemradio or menuitemcheckbox with aria-checked.
a11y.r3: The trigger carries aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded.
a11y.focusBody: On closing, focus returns to the trigger — after Esc and after a selection alike. Without that return, focus lands at the top of the page and the journey through it starts over.

page.title: Context Menu
page.description: Opens on right-click at the cursor position and flips inward at the edges.

demo.areaHint: Rechtsklick in diesen Bereich öffnet das Kontextmenü
demo.areaRich: Rechtsklick zeigt Überschrift, Untermenü und Trenner
demo.areaDisabled: Hier gilt das Menü des Browsers

overview.basicBody: The menu opens at the cursor position. A click outside, Esc and a selection close it again; so do scrolling and resizing the window, because the position would no longer hold.
overview.flipBody: If there is not enough room to the right or below, the menu flips to the other side of the cursor instead of running out of view. Try right-clicking close to the right window edge.
overview.entriesBody: The entries are the same as in the dropdown — including heading, divider, shortcut, destructive action and one level of submenu.
overview.disabledBody: When disabled, the browser takes the right-click back. That is the right state for areas where text is meant to be selected and copied.

usage.whenBody: For actions belonging to a specific object — a table row, a card, an appointment in the calendar. The context menu is always the shortcut, never the only way.
usage.discoverBody: A right-click is invisible: it does not exist on touch devices, and many people never look for it. Every action in the context menu must therefore also be reachable visibly, for example through a kebab trigger in the same row.
usage.c1: Only actions that relate to the object clicked.
usage.c2: The most common action on top, destructive ones at the bottom and separated.
usage.c3: Keep it short — anything beyond about eight entries belongs in a visible toolbar.
usage.dont1: Offer actions exclusively through right-click.
usage.dont2: Capture the context menu over text areas where people copy.
usage.dont3: Use it as a replacement for a visible toolbar.

code.title: Context menu in code
code.basicDesc: The right-click area is the child, the actions come as items:
code.disabledDesc: Disabled hands the right-click back to the browser:

a11y.keyboardBody: Once the menu is open the same paths apply as in the dropdown, because both use the same menu surface:
a11y.k1: Arrows move, Home and End jump to the ends.
a11y.k2: Typing jumps to the matching entry.
a11y.parallelBody: Opening itself hangs on the right-click and is therefore reachable neither by keyboard nor on touch devices. That is why every action needs a second, visible path — otherwise it simply does not exist for part of your users.
a11y.rolesBody: The surface carries role=menu with a label through ariaLabel, the entries carry role=menuitem. An invisible layer above the page catches the click outside and closes the menu.

page.title: Menu Buttons
page.description: Three forms for actions with variants: MenuButton, SplitButton and IconMenuButton. One size, 40px high.

overview.formsBody: All three open the same menu surface and differ in how much they show up front.
overview.f1: MenuButton — one button that only opens the menu. There is no action without a choice.
overview.f2: SplitButton — the main action on the left runs directly, the menu on the right carries the variants.
overview.f3: IconMenuButton — icon only, 40px square, for toolbars and table rows.
overview.variantsBody: primary carries the action colour and belongs to the most important action in a view; neutral is the restrained form with a border. As with the button: only one primary action per view.
overview.splitBody: The two halves share one hit area and are separated by a seam: in the primary variant a light inner line, in the neutral one the shared border. The left half fires immediately without opening the menu.
overview.iconBody: Without a label an ariaLabel is mandatory — otherwise the button is unnamed. The default is the kebab icon in the neutral variant.
overview.alignBody: The menu aligns to the left or right of the button. At the right edge of a view use end.
overview.disabledBody: When disabled both halves are locked — on the SplitButton that includes the main action, not just the menu.

usage.w1: If there is no sensible default action, it is a MenuButton.
usage.w2: If there is a clear main action and less common variants of it, it is a SplitButton.
usage.w3: If there is no room for a label, it is an IconMenuButton — in table rows and toolbars.
usage.splitBody: The SplitButton promises that the left half is the right choice for most cases. If that is not true, people pick wrongly by accident — then the MenuButton is the more honest form.
usage.variantBody: Where several menu buttons sit side by side, at most one carries the primary variant. All others are neutral, otherwise they compete for the same attention.
usage.dont1: Put the SplitButton's main action into its menu as well.
usage.dont2: Use an IconMenuButton without an ariaLabel.
usage.dont3: Make a destructive action the main action of a SplitButton.

code.title: Menu buttons in code
code.menuButtonDesc: A button that only opens the menu:
code.splitDesc: Main action through onClick, variants through items and onSelect:
code.iconDesc: Icon only — the label comes through ariaLabel:

a11y.l1: On the IconMenuButton the ariaLabel is the only label and therefore mandatory.
a11y.l2: On the SplitButton the menu half carries its own menuLabel — otherwise both halves would share one name.
a11y.k1: Arrow down opens the menu from the button.
a11y.k2: Inside the surface the dropdown paths apply: arrows, Home and End, typing, Enter and Esc.
a11y.k3: On the SplitButton, Tab reaches the main action first and then the menu half.
a11y.stateBody: The menu half carries aria-haspopup=menu and aria-expanded; on closing, focus returns to it, not to the main action.

page.title: List
page.description: Display content in a structured way — bulleted, numbered, or as content rows with an icon. Purely for display: nothing in it is clickable.

overview.variantsBody: unordered for collections without an order, ordered only when the order means something — the numerals are then set in DM Mono. content is the row form with title, explanation, and an optional icon.
overview.nestedBody: One level is possible, no deeper. Anything that would need further structure calls for headings or an Accordion.
overview.flushBody: Content rows are separated by thin lines. When the list already sits inside a bordered card, flush removes them.
overview.sizesBody: md is the default at 16 px, sm sets the text at 14 px and reduces the spacing — for data-heavy areas.
overview.keyValueBody: KeyValueList shows the details of one object: the label on the left, the value on the right. With numeric, figures, amounts, IDs, and dates are set in DM Mono with tabular numerals. In narrow columns, layout="stacked" places both below each other.
overview.emptyBody: emptyText explains what will appear here — never just “No data”. The action that creates it sits next to the list, not in the text.

usage.whenBody: For structured, uniform content that is only read. As soon as rows navigate or select, it is a ContainedList; for data rows with columns, a table.
usage.orderBody: Use ordered only when the order means something — steps or a ranking. With an arbitrary order, numbers mislead.
usage.nestingBody: One level at most. Nesting deeper loses the overview the list was meant to create.
usage.numbersBody: Mark amounts, IDs, and dates with numeric so they line up in DM Mono. When a value is missing, an em dash stands there, never an empty cell.
usage.do1: Use it for structured, uniform content
usage.do2: Nest only where there is real hierarchy, one level at most
usage.do3: Use sm for data-heavy areas
usage.dont1: Put clickable rows into a List — use ContainedList
usage.dont2: Replace a table with many columns by a list
usage.dont3: Set amounts or IDs in DM Sans

a11y.semanticBody: unordered renders a ul, ordered an ol, KeyValueList a dl with dt and dd. Screen readers therefore announce the number of entries and the relationship between label and value.
a11y.staticBody: The list contains no buttons and no focus target. When a row needs to be clickable, ContainedList is the right component — making a List focusable afterwards breaks the semantics.
a11y.iconBody: The icon of a content row is decorative and echoes the title. It carries no label of its own; the message is in the text.

page.title: Contained list
page.description: Interactive rows in a bordered card — for navigating or selecting, with icon or avatar, description, meta, and a row action.

demo.title: Settings
demo.m2Desc: Delivery on the next working day

overview.modesBody: navigation leads onwards: every row opens a target, with a chevron on the right. single and multiple select — a radio or checkbox sits on the left and the chosen row rests on the selection surface. One mode per list.
overview.rowBody: The title is required, everything else optional:
overview.row1: description explains the row, it does not repeat it
overview.row2: meta sits on the right in DM Mono for a date, count, or amount
overview.row3: avatar carries two letters, icon sits in a tinted surface
overview.row4: action replaces the chevron and does not open the row
overview.groupsBody: groups instead of items sets headings in mono capitals that stay at the top while scrolling — by alphabet, date, or category. The heading itself is never clickable.
overview.sizesBody: md is the default, sm condenses row height, icon, and text for compact areas.
overview.emptyBody: emptyText explains what will appear here and does not apologise. The action that creates it sits next to or below the card, not as an empty row inside it.

usage.whenBody: For clickable or selectable rows in a clearly bounded container. When the list needs columns, sorting, or bulk actions, it is a table. When nothing is clickable, it is a List.
usage.oneModeBody: Navigating and selecting are never mixed. If both are needed, split the list or move the selection into its own view.
usage.actionBody: At most one action per row. It stops the click, so it does not open the row, and needs its own aria-label. Several actions belong in a menu.
usage.emptyBody: The text names what will appear here. “No data” says nothing about the next step.
usage.do1: Use it for clickable or selectable rows in a bounded container
usage.do2: Use groups with sticky headings for long, sorted lists
usage.do3: Use sm in dense, data-heavy areas
usage.dont1: Mix navigation and multiple selection in the same list
usage.dont2: Make the row clickable and offer several links inside it
usage.dont3: Show the selection through the background colour alone

a11y.rolesBody: navigation renders role="list", the selection modes role="listbox" with role="option" and aria-selected per row. With multiple, the list also carries aria-multiselectable. ariaLabel names what the list is about.
a11y.key1: Arrow up and down — move the focus only, they do not select
a11y.key2: Enter or Space — activates the focused row
a11y.key3: Home and End — jump to the start and to the end
a11y.actionBody: The action carries its own aria-label and sits outside the row's tab order. Without actionLabel it reads “More actions”.

page.title: Pagination
page.description: Pages through a set that does not fit on one screen. It is both position and control: you must be able to see where you are and how much is still to come.

overview.variantsBody: numbers is the normal case below a list or a set of cards. bar belongs under a table: entries per page and the range on the left, the numbers and, with many pages, the direct jump on the right. compact is for narrow columns and mobile.
overview.windowBody: The first and last page are always visible, around the current one stand as many neighbours as siblings specifies, with an ellipsis in between. The bar therefore barely changes width while paging.
overview.statesBody: At the edges, previous and next are disabled, not hidden — the bar keeps its shape. The active page is filled and carries aria-current.
overview.sizesBody: Hit targets are 40 px at md and 32 px at sm. Use md on touch surfaces.

usage.whenBody: For long, clearly divided result sets: tables, search results, sets of cards. When the list loads more while scrolling, there is no pagination — the two do not go together.
usage.positionBody: The bar sits below the set it refers to. After a page change the view stays at the top of the list; the page does not jump into the middle.
usage.pageSizeBody: When the number per page changes, the view returns to page 1. That belongs in the call: onPageSizeChange sets both size and page.
usage.numeralsBody: All figures are set in DM Mono with tabular numerals so they do not shift while paging. When the total is known, it is shown.
usage.do1: Mark the current page clearly and show the range “X–Y of Z”
usage.do2: Use an ellipsis with many pages instead of showing every number
usage.do3: Use the compact form on narrow layouts
usage.dont1: Mark the active page by bold type alone
usage.dont2: Hide previous and next at the edges instead of disabling them
usage.dont3: Combine pagination with infinite scrolling

a11y.navBody: The bar is a nav with aria-label. Every number is a button with a label such as “Page 4”, the ellipsis is aria-hidden and not focusable.
a11y.currentBody: The active page carries aria-current="page" and is filled. The marking therefore does not rest on colour alone.
a11y.targetBody: The buttons measure 40 px at md and 32 px at sm. On touch surfaces md is the right choice.

page.description: KPI cards with label, pre-formatted value, and optional delta display (up / down / neutral).

overview.anatomyBody: StatCard consists of four sections — label and value are always visible, delta is optional.
overview.an1: label — uppercase identifier for the metric (e.g. 'Active Users')
overview.an3: delta — optional comparison value with direction indicator (↑/↓/→)
overview.demoBody: 4 StatCards: up (green), up (green), down (red), and no delta.

usage.title: When to use StatCard?
usage.intro: StatCards suit KPI dashboards and metrics overviews where a single metric needs to be grasped at a glance.
usage.formatBody: The component performs no number formatting — value and delta are passed as strings. Formatting (currency, unit, thousands separator) happens in the calling component, e.g. via Intl.NumberFormat.
usage.do1: Pass values as pre-formatted strings (e.g. '€84.2k', '12,847')
usage.do2: Set deltaDir correctly: up = positive increase, down = negative decline
usage.do3: Arrange StatCards in a grid with consistent width per row (4 columns)
usage.dont1: No raw numbers without formatting
usage.dont2: Don't leave delta empty when deltaDir is set — no delta section will be shown
usage.dont3: No overly long labels — max 2–3 words for the uppercase line
usage.doNote: StatCards for quickly readable single metrics.
usage.dontNote: No StatCard for complex datasets — use Table.

code.title: Code Examples
code.baseDesc: label, value, delta, and deltaDir — all four props.
code.noDeltaDesc: Without the delta prop, no delta section is shown. deltaDir='neutral' shows gray with →.
code.gridDesc: 4-column grid — standard layout for KPI dashboards.
code.formatDesc: Formatting happens outside the component — pass a pre-formatted string.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: StatCards are static display elements. Screen readers read label, value, and delta as regular text — no special ARIA handling needed, provided delta icons have text alternatives.
a11y.iconBody: ↑ / ↓ / → are Unicode characters that screen readers read aloud. If meaning is unclear, add a visually hidden span with aria-label='Increase' / 'Decrease'.
a11y.ariaBody: For icon-only deltas (no text), set aria-label on the delta element: aria-label='Increase of 4.2 percent'. For combined strings (↑ 4.2%) no further ARIA is needed.
a11y.colorTitle: Color is not the only indicator
a11y.colorBody: up (green) / down (red) / neutral (gray) communicate direction via color. The arrow symbol (↑/↓/→) ensures direction is also recognizable without color — WCAG 1.4.1 compliant.

page.description: Progress bar for loading operations, file uploads, and multi-step processes.

overview.anatomyBody: Progress consists of a track and an indicator showing current progress. Optional label and value elements complement the bar.
overview.an1: Track — gray background bar as full width
overview.an3: Label — optional description text left above the bar
overview.an4: Value — optional percentage display right above the bar (showValue)
overview.an5: size — bar thickness: sm (4 px), md (6 px), lg (10 px)
overview.variantsBody: Five color variants for different contexts: neutral (default), accent (orange), success (green), warning (yellow), error (red).
overview.sizesBody: Three sizes control bar thickness. md is the default for most use cases.
overview.showValueBody: showValue displays the current percentage right above the bar. Can be combined with label.

usage.title: When to use Progress?
usage.intro: Progress suits operations with a known endpoint: file uploads, form steps, and load progress. The value prop must always hold a concrete 0–100 value.
usage.whenNotBody: For unknown loading times (indeterminate state), Skeleton is more appropriate. Progress always communicates concrete progress — never use it for general loading states without a percentage value.
usage.do1: Set the label prop to explain the context of the progress
usage.do2: Use variant semantically: success on completion, error on failure
usage.do3: Use showValue in upload dialogs where the exact percentage is helpful
usage.dont1: Don't use Progress for indeterminate states — use Skeleton instead
usage.dont2: Don't animate value upward without real progress behind it
usage.dont3: Don't place multiple progress bars side by side without labels
usage.doNote: Progress for measurable, controlled progress states.
usage.dontNote: No Progress for loading states without a concrete percentage value.

code.title: Code Examples
code.baseDesc: Minimal usage — value is the only required prop (0–100).
code.variantsDesc: Five variants with label prop for contextual colors.
code.sizesDesc: sm / md (default) / lg — control bar thickness.
code.showValueDesc: Combines label (left) and percentage (right) above the bar.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: Radix sets role='progressbar', aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax automatically. A descriptive label is mandatory for screen readers.
a11y.roleBody: Radix UI sets role='progressbar' automatically on the root element. No manual ARIA attribute needed.
a11y.ariaBody: Radix sets aria-valuenow={value}, aria-valuemin={0}, aria-valuemax={100} automatically. Screen readers announce e.g. '75%'.
a11y.labelBody: Without the label prop, aria-label must be set on the Progress element so screen readers understand the context: 'Upload in progress: 75%'.
a11y.colorTitle: Color is not the only indicator
a11y.colorBody: The variant color (green/red/yellow) alone is insufficient. The label text must also communicate the state linguistically — WCAG 1.4.1 compliant.

page.description: User representation via image or initials — individually or as a group.

overview.anatomyBody: Avatar shows either an image (src) or an initials fallback. AvatarGroup stacks multiple avatars with an automatic overflow counter.
overview.an1: Image — image variant via src prop with alt text
overview.an2: Fallback — initials variant with optional background color (color/textColor)
overview.an3: Size — xs (24 px) to xl (56 px) via size prop
overview.sizesBody: Five sizes from xs to xl. md (40 px) is the standard for list rows and comments.
overview.fallbackBody: When no src is provided, Avatar shows initials. With color/textColor the background color is controlled; without color the system fallback color applies.
overview.groupBody: AvatarGroup shows up to max avatars — excess is shown as '+N'. Demo: 6 avatars with max=4 → 4 visible + '+2'.

usage.title: When to use Avatar?
usage.intro: Avatar suits user identification in lists, comments, profile headers, and team views. Use the initials fallback when no image is available.
usage.groupMaxBody: max=4 or max=5 is the recommended range for AvatarGroup. With more visible avatars, readability decreases. The '+N' count informs about the total number.
usage.do1: Always set alt text for src avatars (e.g. alt='Alice Jones')
usage.do2: Use initials fallback with color/textColor for consistent brand assignment
usage.do3: Use AvatarGroup for team membership and participant lists
usage.dont1: No src without alt attribute — screen readers cannot describe the image
usage.dont2: Don't show more than 5 avatars without overflow — use AvatarGroup with max
usage.dont3: Don't mix avatar sizes within an AvatarGroup
usage.doNote: Avatar for person identification with a clear fallback strategy.
usage.dontNote: No avatar without a text alternative for screen readers.

code.title: Code Examples
code.sizesDesc: All five sizes from xs to xl with initials.
code.imageDesc: src variant — alt text is required.
code.groupDesc: 6 avatars, max=4 — shows 4 avatars + '+2' overflow counter.
code.noColorDesc: Without color the system fallback applies. With color/textColor explicit brand assignment.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: Avatars are visual elements. Screen readers need text alternatives — either via alt (src variant) or aria-label (initials variant in contextless use).
a11y.altBody: For Avatar with src always set alt='Full Name'. Empty alt (alt='') only when the avatar is purely decorative and the name already appears in surrounding text.
a11y.ariaBody: When Avatar shows only initials and no surrounding context names the person, set aria-label='Alice Jones' on the avatar.
a11y.overflowBody: The overflow counter '+N' needs aria-label='N more participants' so screen readers understand the meaning.

page.description: Loading placeholder for content that is not yet available.

overview.anatomyBody: Skeleton is a pulsing placeholder that mimics the shape of the expected content. Three variants cover text, circles (avatar), and rectangles (images/cards).
overview.an2: width / height — width and height as number (px) or CSS string ('60%')
overview.an3: animate-pulse — pulsing animation via Tailwind (always active)
overview.an4: aria-hidden='true' — Skeleton is invisible to screen readers (set in component)
overview.variantsBody: text for paragraphs, circle for avatar placeholders, rect for images and card blocks.
overview.cardBody: SkeletonCard is a pre-configured composition: Avatar + 2 text lines, rect block, and 3 descending text lines — max-w-[360px].

usage.title: When to use Skeleton?
usage.intro: Skeleton suits initial loading of content whose structure is known: lists, cards, profile pages. The placeholder should closely match the shape of the real content.
usage.whenNotBody: For error and empty states, Alert and EmptyState are more appropriate. Skeleton signals 'loading soon' — not 'nothing found' or 'error occurred'.
usage.do1: Match skeleton shapes to the real content (size, number of lines)
usage.do2: Use SkeletonCard for card layouts — saves composition effort
usage.do3: Set aria-live='polite' outside the skeleton to announce when loading ends
usage.dont1: Don't use Skeleton for known error or empty states
usage.dont2: Don't show Skeleton indefinitely — show an error state after timeout
usage.dont3: Don't ignore skeleton animations for users with prefers-reduced-motion
usage.doNote: Skeleton for loading states with a known content structure.
usage.dontNote: No Skeleton as a permanent state without timeout logic.

code.title: Code Examples
code.textDesc: Descending text lines simulate a paragraph — decreasing width for a more natural look.
code.circleDesc: Round placeholders for avatar elements in various sizes.
code.rectDesc: Rectangular placeholders for images, hero areas, and card blocks.
code.cardDesc: Ready-made composition without props — for standard card layouts.
code.compositeDesc: Combine individual skeleton elements into a list row (circle + 2 text lines).

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: Skeleton elements are purely visual — aria-hidden='true' is already set in the component. Screen readers automatically skip them. For the loading announcement, aria-live outside the skeleton is needed.
a11y.hiddenBody: The Skeleton component sets aria-hidden='true' internally. No manual ARIA attribute needed — screen readers skip the placeholder.
a11y.liveBody: A container with aria-live='polite' outside the skeleton announces the end of loading: e.g. 'Content loaded'. This informs screen reader users.
a11y.motionBody: animate-pulse animates the skeleton. Users with prefers-reduced-motion have reduced animations in their OS. Tailwind's animate-pulse respects this setting automatically in modern browsers.

page.title: Date Picker
page.description: Date selection component with a calendar popover and localization support

overview.anatomyBody: The DatePicker consists of a trigger button and a calendar popover. The popover closes automatically after a date is selected.
overview.variantsBody: Five variants are available: default (single day), range (date range), withTime (date + time), inline (always-visible calendar), and input (keyboard entry with calendar icon).
overview.localeBody: The displayed date is automatically formatted according to the active language: German (de-DE) or English (en-US).

usage.title: Usage
usage.intro: The DatePicker is a controlled component — pass the current value via value and handle changes via onChange.
usage.rangeBody: The range variant expects an object { from, to } as value and returns the same format.
usage.withTimeBody: The withTime variant adds a time input below the calendar. The onChange callback returns a full Date object including hours and minutes.
usage.inlineBody: The inline variant renders the calendar directly — without a popover trigger. Use it for embedded forms where prominent date selection is needed.
usage.inputBody: The input variant combines a DD/MM/YYYY text field with a calendar icon button. Slashes are inserted automatically as the user types. The calendar icon opens a popover for visual date selection.
usage.disabledBody: Use the disabledDates prop to exclude specific dates from selection, such as holidays or already booked dates.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: The DatePicker is built on Radix UI Popover and react-day-picker with full keyboard navigation.
a11y.keyboardBody: Enter/Space opens the popover. Inside the calendar, arrow keys navigate between days, Enter selects a date, and Escape closes the popover.

page.title: Loading Indicator
page.description: Visual feedback for background operations in three variants

overview.anatomyBody: The LoadingIndicator is a purely visual component with no interactive elements. It signals to the user that a background operation is in progress.
overview.variantsBody: Three variants are available: Spinner (rotating circle border), Bar (pulsing horizontal bar), and Dots (three bouncing dots).

usage.title: Usage
usage.intro: Use a Loading Indicator when an operation takes longer than 300ms. Very short operations do not require an indicator.
usage.variantGuideBody: Spinner suits general loading states. Bar fits progress feedback in forms. Dots works well for inline loading states inside text or buttons.

code.title: Code
code.basicDesc: Select the variant via the variant prop.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: Add an aria-label to the LoadingIndicator so screen readers can announce the loading state.
a11y.motionBody: Tailwind's animate-* classes automatically respect the operating system's prefers-reduced-motion setting.

page.title: Upload Field
page.description: File input component in three variants: default, drag-and-drop, and preview

overview.anatomyBody: The UploadField consists of a hidden native file input and a visual trigger. The trigger opens the browser's file dialog.
overview.variantsBody: default: simple button. dropzone: drag-and-drop area with drag-over state. preview: shows the filename after selection.

usage.title: Usage
usage.intro: Use UploadField wherever users need to select a file. Choose the variant based on available space and context.
usage.variantGuideBody: default for compact forms, dropzone for prominent upload areas, preview when the selected filename should remain visible.

code.title: Code
code.basicDesc: Select the variant via the variant prop.

a11y.title: Accessibility
a11y.intro: The trigger button is keyboard-focusable. The hidden native input is activated by clicking the trigger.
a11y.keyboardBody: Tab focuses the trigger; Enter or Space opens the file dialog.

dropzone.hint: Drag a file here or click to browse

page.title: Tooltip
page.description: A short explanation on hover or focus. Purely informative, never interactive.

demo.title: Tastenkürzel
demo.richContent: Öffnet die Suche von überall — auch aus Untermenüs.
demo.taxContent: Nach § 19 UStG wird keine Umsatzsteuer ausgewiesen.

overview.placementBody: Four placements. If there is not enough room on the requested side, the tooltip flips to the opposite side; the arrow stays aligned to the centre of the trigger.
overview.variantsBody: Without title you get the one-line explanation. With title you get the two-line variant for cases where a keyword and a sentence belong together.
overview.triggerBody: Exactly one child that can take a ref and is focusable. A span as a trigger needs tabIndex={0}, otherwise the tooltip is unreachable for keyboard users.
overview.b1: With a mouse the tooltip opens after about 400ms so it does not flash while passing over.
overview.b2: On keyboard focus it opens immediately, because nothing there is incidental.
overview.b4: It is attached to body so no container with overflow: hidden can clip it.

usage.whenBody: For buttons that carry only an icon, and for terms that need one line of explanation. As soon as something inside would be clickable — a link, a button, a form field — it is a popover, not a tooltip: the tooltip accepts no mouse and disappears as soon as you move towards it.
usage.contentBody: A hint, not a paragraph. What a person needs in order to work belongs visibly on the page — never in a tooltip alone.
usage.touchBody: There is no hover on touch devices. A tooltip must never be the only source of information there.
usage.dont1: Put links or buttons inside the tooltip.
usage.dont2: Show important information only there.
usage.dont3: Use it as the only source of explanation on touch devices.
usage.dont4: Use a trigger that cannot receive focus.
usage.dont5: Use the tooltip as a replacement for an aria-label.

code.title: Tooltip in code
code.richDesc: With title you get the two-line variant:
code.spanDesc: A trigger that is not focusable needs tabIndex:

a11y.focusBody: The tooltip opens on keyboard focus without delay and closes when focus leaves. The trigger must be focusable, otherwise the explanation cannot be reached by keyboard.
a11y.a1: The tooltip carries role="tooltip" and is tied to the trigger through aria-describedby.
a11y.a2: An icon button with aria-label keeps its label — the tooltip is the visible addition, not the replacement.
a11y.a3: The tooltip accepts no mouse, so moving towards it does not take the explanation away.
a11y.limitsBody: The tooltip is not interactive. Content meant to be clicked, copied or read belongs in a popover or on the page.

page.title: Slider
page.description: Set a value continuously or in steps — when the approximate position matters more than the exact number.

overview.basicBody: Without ticks and step labels the handle runs freely. The value display above the track shows the value permanently, the dark bubble only while dragging and on keyboard focus.
overview.sizesBody: The handle is white with a thin border and casts a light shadow — it should sit above the track, not disappear into it.
overview.discreteBody: In discrete mode 4px dots mark the steps and the step labels name them below the track. The active step uses the text colour, the rest are muted; the bubble then shows the step name instead of the number.
overview.minMaxBody: Minimum and maximum sit below the ends of the track. The step determines which values the handle snaps to.
overview.iconsBody: Icons at the ends show the direction of the quantity. They do not replace a label — without a visible label the slider needs an ariaLabel.
overview.controlledBody: onChange fires while dragging, onChangeEnd only on release — for expensive updates such as server requests. Drag the handle and let go: the value below only follows afterwards.
overview.verticalBody: Use the vertical orientation only when the quantity itself is thought of vertically — brightness, level. The value bubble then appears to the right of the handle.
overview.disabledBody: When disabled, track and handle stay visible but accept neither pointer nor keyboard.

usage.whenBody: When the approximate position matters more than the exact number: volume, brightness, radius, price range. If the value must be exact or typeable, a number field belongs next to it — or it is just a number field to begin with.
usage.valueBody: The bubble does not replace a permanent value display: it only appears while dragging and on focus. Where the value should stay visible, put the value display next to it or couple it with a number field.
usage.stepBody: For a few named steps — three, four — a radio is clearer than a slider. More than about ten visible ticks becomes restless and helps nobody hit a value.
usage.changeEndBody: If the change triggers a server request or a costly recalculation, it belongs in onChangeEnd — otherwise it fires on every pixel of the drag.
usage.dont1: Use a slider for values that must be hit exactly.
usage.dont2: Show the value bubble permanently.
usage.dont3: Show more than about ten visible ticks.
usage.dont4: Use it without a label or ariaLabel.

code.title: Slider in code
code.basicDesc: Range through min, max and step; the value display through showValue:
code.discreteDesc: Discrete mode comes from showTicks and stepLabels:
code.formatDesc: formatValue drives bubble, value display and aria-valuetext together:
code.verticalDesc: Vertical with icons at the ends:

a11y.k1: Arrow keys move the value by one step.
a11y.k2: Page Up and Page Down move it by a tenth of the range.
a11y.k3: Home and End jump to the ends.
a11y.a1: The handle carries role="slider" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuenow.
a11y.a2: Named steps and custom formatting come through aria-valuetext — otherwise a screen reader would read out the bare number.
a11y.a3: Without a visible label an ariaLabel is mandatory.
a11y.targetBody: The track has padding above and below so the hit target is larger than the visible 6px. A click on the track jumps to that value instead of only accepting the handle.

page.intro: med.o specialises in developing software products for the medical sector.
page.body1: The med.o Design System provides a collection of reusable UI components, design decisions, and guidelines that enable consistent and accessible user interfaces.

brand.title: Brand
brand.description: Wordmark and iconography: how the medo logo is used and which icon source the system relies on.

wordmark.title: Wordmark
wordmark.body: The medo logo appears as a wordmark. The dot is always primary-600 and is never recoloured or removed.
wordmark.inverted: Inverted on dark surfaces, the dot comes along

icons.title: Iconography
icons.body: The system has exactly one icon source: Material Symbols Rounded, weight 300, FILL 0. Custom SVG icons, emojis and other icon libraries are ruled out.
icons.sizesBody: 18 px next to text-sm, 20 px next to text-base, 24 px standalone. Smaller values appear only where a component's specification sets them itself.

usage.logo1: Never show the wordmark below 24 px in height.
usage.logo2: Use the inverted version on dark surfaces.
usage.logo3: Never distort the aspect ratio and never recolour the mark.
usage.logo4: Embed it as SVG so the mark stays sharp at any resolution.
usage.icons1: Material Symbols Rounded only, weight 300, FILL 0.
usage.icons2: Always go through the Icon component, never inline SVG.
usage.icons3: Action components such as Button and Link set their main icon to 20, 22 or 24 px depending on size.
usage.icons4: Field and display components keep the icon sizes from their specification.
usage.icons5: Operable icons inside fields get icon-button styling and an aria-label; decorative icons sit flat in the text.

tokens.title: Icon and brand tokens
tokens.body: The tokens that colour the wordmark and the icons. Values come from the loaded token chain.

a11y.1: The wordmark carries the alternative text “medo”.
a11y.2: Operable icons need an aria-label naming the action — not the icon.
a11y.3: Decorative icons are hidden from screen readers.
a11y.4: Operable icon areas keep a hit target of at least 44 × 44 px.
a11y.title: Accessibility

brandColors.title: Colors · Tier 1 Brand
brandColors.description: The raw scales of the system: 15 scales of 12 steps each, from 50 to 1100. Step 600 is the vivid solid colour.

chromatic.title: Chromatic scales
chromatic.body: Thirteen chromatic scales with muted chroma. Every scale runs from 50 to 1100; step 600 carries the solid colour that actions and status draw on.

neutral.title: Neutral scales
neutral.body: Two neutrals: stone is warm and forms the base for surfaces, text and borders. grey is purely neutral and stays reserved for cool contexts.

absolute.title: Absolute colours
absolute.body: White and black sit outside the scales. White is the base surface of the system.

steps.title: The twelve steps
steps.body: Every step has a typical use. It is guidance, not a rigid rule — tier 2 and tier 3 build on it.

legend.s50: Lightest surfaces, such as the page background
legend.s600: Vivid solid colour, mostly for actions

usage.whenBody: Tier 1 is the source, not the working tier. Components use it only where a specification names a brand step itself.
usage.when1: For surfaces, text and borders reach for the semantic tokens of tier 3 first.
usage.when2: If a role needs the full scale, the way there is tier 2.
usage.when3: Direct brand steps stay reserved for special cases such as data visualisation or illustration.
usage.namingBody: A token is called --medo-color-<scale>-<step>, for example --medo-color-teal-600. Steps run from 50 through 100 up to 1100.
usage.rolesBody: Seven of the fifteen scales carry a role on tier 2. The others stand by as reserve.

tokens.title: All brand tokens
tokens.body: Every scale with the values the browser resolves from the loaded token chain.

a11y.1: On a white surface only the dark steps carry enough contrast for text; 1000 and 1100 are the text steps.
a11y.2: Steps 50 to 500 are surface colours, not text colours.
a11y.3: White text sits on a 600 solid surface — except amber, which needs the dark text.
a11y.4: Colour alone never carries a message; status is also conveyed through text and icon.
a11y.title: Accessibility

aliasColors.title: Colors · Tier 2 Alias
aliasColors.description: Seven roles, each with a full twelve-step scale. A role points at exactly one brand scale.

scales.title: The seven roles
scales.body: Every role keeps the full scale and points at exactly one brand scale. If primary later moves from teal to another colour, a single reference changes — and the whole system follows.

mapping.title: Mapping at a glance
mapping.body: Which role sits on which brand scale, and what it stands for.

roles.neutral: Cool neutral for surfaces, text and borders
roles.neutral-alt: Warm neutral — the base neutral of this system

noSecondary.title: No secondary role
noSecondary.body: The system deliberately has no secondary role. Secondary actions come from the neutral action tokens on tier 3, not from a second brand colour.

usage.whyTitle: What the alias tier is for
usage.whyBody: The alias tier gives the raw colours a meaning without already fixing a place in the interface.
usage.why1: Changing a role is a changed reference, not a search and replace.
usage.why2: Roles carry the full scale so tier 3 can reach every step.
usage.why3: As a rule, components do not access tier 2 directly.
usage.neutralBody: neutral-alt points at stone and is the base neutral of the system — surfaces, text and borders come from here. neutral points at grey and stays reserved for cool contexts.
usage.layerBody: Brand supplies the values, alias assigns the role, semantic names the place of use. Components work on tier 3.

tokens.title: All alias tokens
tokens.body: Every role with its twelve steps and the brand step it points at.

a11y.1: Role colours keep the same contrast ratios as the brand scales they point at.
a11y.2: error, warning, success and info always appear together with text and icon, never as colour alone.
a11y.3: warning is the only role carrying dark text on its solid surface.
a11y.title: Accessibility

semanticColors.title: Colors · Tier 3 Semantic
semanticColors.description: The tokens components are built from. Material naming, warm base neutral, white base surface.

applied.title: In use
applied.body: This card is built entirely from semantic tokens — surface, text, border, action and status.

example.heading: Invoice overview
example.body: Every surface, text and border on this card comes from the semantic tokens.
example.caption: surface · text · border · action · success

groups.title: The token groups
groups.body: Every token names the alias step it points at and the value the browser resolves from it.

usage.ruleBody: Components and pages use semantic tokens exclusively. They name the place of use, not the colour.
usage.rule1: Set surface, text, border and icon through the token of their role.
usage.rule2: The base surface is white; surface-container puts a layer underneath.
usage.rule3: Borders stay restrained: border-subtle separates, border encloses, border-strong emphasises.
usage.rule4: Field borders are always 1 px — at rest as well as on focus.
usage.states1: Hover lays a warm surface under the element instead of lightening it.
usage.states2: The focus ring is 3 px wide and uses focus-ring; the destructive variant uses focus-ring-danger.
usage.states3: Selected elements sit on state-selected, not on a solid surface.
usage.states4: Disabled elements use the disabled tokens, never reduced opacity.
usage.statusBody: Every status brings a surface, a border, a text colour and a solid colour.
usage.status1: Messages use surface, border and text; the solid colour stays reserved for dots, icons and buttons.
usage.status2: warning-on-solid is dark because amber is too light for white text.
usage.status3: Status is never conveyed by colour alone — text and icon belong to it.

tokens.title: All semantic tokens
tokens.body: Every group with token name, resolved value and the alias step the token points at.

a11y.1: The combinations of text and surface tokens are checked against WCAG 2.2 AA.
a11y.2: text-disabled and icon-disabled are deliberately low in contrast and appear only on non-operable elements.
a11y.3: The focus ring is visible on every operable element and is never removed.
a11y.4: Links are recognisable by their underline in addition to colour.
a11y.5: Status colours always appear together with text and icon.
a11y.title: Accessibility

typography.title: Typography
typography.description: DM Sans for interface and text, DM Mono for data and labels. A scale at ratio 1.25 from 16 px.

families.title: Font families
families.body: Two families, no more. DM Sans carries body text, labels and headings. DM Mono stands for numbers, amounts, IDs, dates and code.

scale.title: Scale
scale.body: Ratio 1.25 (major third), base 16 px, t-shirt sizes from xs to 4xl. From text-xl upwards the tracking tightens to −0.02em.

weights.title: Weights
weights.body: Four weights. In the interface, headings carry 600; button labels always stay at 400.

rhythm.title: Line height and tracking
rhythm.leadingSample: Consistent line heights keep paragraphs calm and readable across every text size.

applied.title: In use
applied.heading: A system that starts with the content
applied.lead: Typography carries the voice of the product. Clear hierarchy, calm lines and reliable sizes make every surface readable at once.
applied.body: The 1.25 ratio gives enough contrast between the levels without making the jumps feel harsh. Body copy at 16 px with generous line height stays comfortable over long stretches. Secondary information recedes through size and colour rather than disappearing.
applied.caption: Caption · text-sm — for metadata, hints and fine detail.

usage.hierarchyBody: Hierarchy comes from size, weight and colour — not from in-between sizes.
usage.hierarchy1: One text-3xl or text-4xl level per page, with text-2xl for sections below it.
usage.hierarchy2: Body copy sits on text-base, secondary text on text-sm.
usage.hierarchy3: text-xs stays reserved for metadata and mono labels.
usage.hierarchy4: Headings from text-xl upwards get tracking-tight.
usage.monoBody: Numbers, amounts, IDs, dates and times are set in DM Mono so digits line up in tables and lists. German formats are mandatory.
usage.rules1: No in-between sizes — every text size sits on the scale.
usage.rules2: Button labels carry weight 400, in every variant and size.
usage.rules3: Button sizes follow the scale: sm text-xs, md text-sm, lg text-base.
usage.rules4: Mono micro labels sit at 11 or 12 px.

tokens.title: Typography tokens
tokens.body: Families, sizes, line heights, weights and tracking with the values from the loaded token chain.

a11y.1: The page stays operable up to 200 % zoom; line heights are defined as a factor and grow along.
a11y.2: Body copy never drops below 16 px.
a11y.3: Lines stay around 60 characters — longer lines make it harder to find the way back.
a11y.4: text-xs is not used for body copy, only for metadata and labels.
a11y.title: Accessibility

foundations.title: Foundations
foundations.description: The invisible frame: a 4 px spacing grid, soft radii, warm shadows, a 12-column grid and restrained motion.

spacing.title: Spacing
spacing.body: Base 4 px, t-shirt names from 3xs to 4xl. Spacing always comes from the scale, never from free values.
spacing.appliedBody: A card with padding lg, inner spacing sm and radius lg.
spacing.demoBody: All locations work from the same data.
spacing.demoCaption: Padding lg · gap sm · radius lg

radii.title: Radii
radii.body: Seven steps from none to full. Chips and tags are always full.

elevation.title: Elevation
elevation.body: Warm, soft shadows based on rgba(31,29,26) — never neutral grey.

borders.title: Border widths
borders.body: Two widths. 1 px is the default; 2 px stays reserved for selected and active indicators.

grid.title: Grid
grid.body: Twelve columns with a 24 px gutter, container at most 1200 px wide.
grid.rule1: Twelve columns divide into 2, 3, 4 and 6 — the usual layouts work out.
grid.rule2: The gutter is space-lg and is not varied per page.
grid.rule3: Beyond 1200 px the margin grows, not the content.

breakpoints.title: Breakpoints
breakpoints.body: Five steps. The documentation itself switches to the mobile view at 768 px.

motion.title: Motion
motion.body: Very restrained. Motion explains a change of state, it does not attract attention.
motion.rule1: State changes run in 120 to 180 ms with ease-out.
motion.rule2: Overlays fade in and out in 180 to 240 ms.
motion.rule3: No bounces, no springs, no attention animations.
motion.rule4: What changes moves — not the whole page.
motion.note: There are no tokens for motion: duration and easing are stated as a rule in the system documentation and are set directly in the components.

usage.spacing1: Inner spacing of cards and dialogs comes from lg or xl.
usage.spacing2: Closely related elements sit at xs to sm.
usage.spacing3: Sections are separated by xl to 3xl.
usage.spacing4: Values that sit on no step are computed from tokens, never hardcoded.
usage.radii1: Chips and tags are always full.
usage.radii3: Every component fixes the remaining steps in its own specification.
usage.elevation1: The step follows the height above the page: sm for resting cards, md for raised elements, lg for popovers and menus, xl for dialogs.
usage.elevation2: The shadow base stays warm; a neutral grey shadow does not fit the stone base neutral.
usage.elevation3: Shadows are never rebuilt by hand, always set through the token.
usage.layout1: Twelve columns, 24 px gutter, container at most 1200 px.
usage.layout2: Operable areas keep at least 44 × 44 px.
usage.layout3: Below 768 px the navigation folds into the mobile view.

tokens.title: Foundation tokens
tokens.body: Spacing, radii, elevation, border widths and breakpoints with the values from the loaded token chain.

a11y.1: Operable elements keep a hit target of at least 44 × 44 px.
a11y.2: Spacing between controls prevents mis-taps on touch devices.
a11y.3: Motion stays short and calm; it never replaces a text message.
a11y.4: The 3 px focus ring needs room — elements never sit so flush to an edge that the ring gets clipped.
